iconicAnchor.label: Unbleached linen and other plant-fiber textiles showing weave, drape, and domestic use
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Natural-fiber spinning, weaving, dyeing, and household textile traditions
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: The V&A traces linen from flax through domestic textile production and use, establishing fiber origin, absorbency, drape, labor, and everyday function as the material's defining context.

sources.title: Linen — the original sustainable material
supports: Linen is made from flax and has long served clothing, bedlinen, underlayers, and other domestic textile uses.
The fiber's absorbency and heat conduction contribute to its characteristic functional and tactile behavior.

sources.title: The Secret Life of Textiles: Plant Fibers — Exhibition Themes
supports: Plant source and processing conditions materially affect a textile's aesthetic and functional qualities.
Linen, hemp, ramie, and cotton have different fiber structures and routes into yarn, supporting a broader natural-textile node rather than linen alone.
